questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to fo to an English speaking country, but I was sure I did not want to go to USA, therefore Canada was an obvious choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I has been really amazing, and I have learned a lot about my own learning, and myself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was not super easy, but people were very sweet and help full.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an international student thing, we could be in contact with. They helped a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I fell like there was a lot of orientation for first years, and it was not divided between first years and international students at all times, this made it difficult to navigate, but nevertheless it worked out fine, and everybody were super sweet and easy going.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I did it with four other girls from DK, and we just searched on Airbnb, it was pretty easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Live closer to the university, and preferably near mason ville and/or just in the north end of town. South London was fine, but it was a pretty long bus ride, and everybody lived in the other end of town.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I fell like the canadian standard was lower than expected, but everything worked out. I head that the on-campus housing was very expensive, and you also needed to provide pillow and sheets yourself. 
All this were in the rented house I lived in. (also stuff lige pans and pots, towels and so on, this were on campus something they expected you to bring yourself, but it was in out rented house)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was easy, but I gave it a lower score as I did not know that I was registered until I asked, but it turned out that this was already sorted out.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just got an email, and filled everything out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
We could write to
goabroad.uwo.ca
, they were very helpful and sweet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I godt almost all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I feel like you can't do it wrong.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think they offered very good academic programs, and the lectures were good. I think maybe it was not as channelling, but this might be partly because I chose a combination of 1,2,3, and 4th year courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one on each year, 1,2,3, and 4th. In Canada the BA is four years long.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching in Canada differed a lot. We had almost no book/reading, only powerpoints. We had a lot of quizzes thought out the course, and small assignments. They also do midterms, in the middle of the semester, which counts for 30-40% of the final grade. You differently have to pay attention through out the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1002A psychology
3592 Principle of human genetics 
4553 Biology of aging. 
2500 microbiology and immunology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biology of aging is my strongest recommendation, Robert is a very good teacher, it combines knowledge we already have in new ways with an interesting perspective. 
The only course I took that I would not recommend necessarily is the 1002A, it was alright and easy, but it was mandatory to be there, and it was a first year course. Remember than in Canada they start university at 18-19, so everybody it very young, and may not be at the same point as yourself.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Western is a party university, and the party street was always busy, even though we did the same 5 clubs. But other than that, it was a pretty small town, and it had some nice markets and you can do escape rooms and stuff like that. However it is very far from Copenhagen. They have a stadium in town were there's a lot of ice hockey games with the London Knights, do that, its fun!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of clubs at university, you can do sports and hiking clubs, or whatever you want. I think maybe there's a 1000 club at campus. Also every sport game is free for students, both ice hockey and football.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think if you play sports a home, come do the same sport here. If you would like to do a lot of hikes, do the out door club. I did not do it myself but I regret not doing it, I think it would have been easier to meet more Canadians.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: We did a lot of traveling, I think I would do like hikes and outdoor activities in the beginning of the semester, and then do the cities, like toronto or montreal in the end. Montreal was very nice to visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do events, even If you think they are silly, it will get you into contact with somebody.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The taxes are not included in the price you see in the supermarked, and also I never got the hang of when to tip and when not to tip.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they were as sweet as promised.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You can have a wonderful time a Western University, but you need to allow yourself to be social. Maybe lower your expectations a bit, you won't be friends with a lot of Canadians, as they are used to take their classes alone, and are fine with it, but spend time with the other exchange and internal students, other Danes, just have fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do the gradclub for quiz nights, and also all exams are written in hand, so bring a pencil.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I got better in my spoken and written language, and maybe that I also learned a lot about how I learn material the best.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping attention thought the course, not necessarily because it was boring, but because we are used to be able to look up the material later, and here we only had the powerpoints, and spoilers, they don't put more text on it. Even though every body is very sweet to share notes, its better to have your own.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
